description.narrative: The project will improve patients' and health workers' safety in hospitals in Mongolia. It will (i) improve the safety of blood transfusions, (ii) strengthen medical waste management, and (iii) prevent and control hospital acquired infections. It complements previous Asian Development Bank (ADB) initiatives in the health sector in Mongolia.

title.narrative: Loan 2963: 100% of contracts awarded and 100% disbursed as of 30 May 2023
Loan 3921: 100% of contracts awarded and 100% disbursed as of 30 May 2023

Progress Toward Outcome: The project assisted in establishment of the new National Center for Transfusion Medicine and 26 blood banks nationwide. The project has accomplished its aim to strengthen the blood safety by ensuring production of safe and quality blood products, capacity building of staff concerned, organizing blood donor management systems and increasing public awareness. the construction of all planned eight medical waste facilities (MWF) were completed. The project completed the renovation of 27 central sterilization departments (CSSDs) and 19 microbiology laboratories. As of 30 April 2022, the project (i) upgraded the laboratory testing capacity of the NCCD through the provision of high-performance analyzers and capacity building training (package G09); (ii) expanded the capacity of intensive care units (ICUs) in 44 referral hospitals in Ulaanbaatar, and aimags (packages G04, G05, G06, G07, and G08, G13 and G14 ) through the provision of fully equipped 210 ICU beds, personal protective equipment (PPE) and capacity building training in the treatment of COVID-19 and SARI patients; (iii) upgraded the capacity of SCH1 and SCH3 through the provision of medical equipment for the treatment of high-risk patients and patients with complications (packages G02, G03, G10, G11, G12 and G15). The project trained 778 (80.2% are women) doctors and nurses in five round of online training conducted in June- July 2021. The project implementation progress is estimated at 99.9% while the time elapsed is 100%. The project has completed the central sterilization service department (CSSD) renovation in Tuv, Bayan-Ulgii, Govi-Altai, Arkhangai, Zavkhan, Govisumber and Dundgovi aimags. The project also completed the installation of sterilization and disinfection equipment in these project sites and Maternal and Child Health Center-2. The on-site practical training on re-processing of surgical instruments and operations of CSSDs is completed, with 83 staff (89.2% women). Design and build for warehouse facility for emergency medicines and supply of angiography system for SCH3 is completed.
Some results are in the Audited Project Financial Statements | Feb 2023: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/45009/45009-002-apfs-en_5.pdf
Some results are in the Proactive Integrity Reviews (PIR) | Jan 2019: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/45009/45009-002-pir-en.pdf
